name: 1638 Prairie Avenue: the brick stable on the alley, K12

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: STANDING IN 1904 rests on two maps either side of it. Robinson's 1886 plate 10 draws a pink, crossed building on the alley behind lot 1 (house number 1638 in its margin, a 40 ft frontage), about 10.8 m deep (columns 343.4-374.6) by 11.5 m along the alley (rows 1332.0-1365.2), half-height edges of pink-density profiles on the committed plate raster at its 0.346 m a pixel, which take in the plate's own border lines (the same profiles return lot 3's stable, 1712's, as its published reading, columns 346.1-370.1 by rows 1455.9-1492.5): within about one of its pixels, the building the 1911 sheet draws, 10.46 by 11.04 m, and the plate leaves the same 1.8 m gap to lot 2's stable south of it that the sheet leaves to 1700-1706's. The 1911 sheet (census row s20-1638-r1) draws it two storeys, brick and crossed. FROM: the record claims the 1904 target and no earlier day. TO: the last day of the year the sheet was published, the latest date anything here shows it standing; it is not a demolition date.

placement.position_note: The middle of the building's alley (west) wall at grade, read off the committed sheet 20 raster (chicago/reference/prairie-avenue/sanborn-1911-and-robinson-1886/sanborn_1911_vol3_sheet_20.jpg) at pixel (2225.60, 3662.99): the alley wall's line by median darkness profiles over rows 3575-3640 and 3700-3755 (peaks at columns 2225.34 and 2225.86), halfway between its north wall line (row 3554.29, on the 1636/1638 lot line, which the same profile east of the building finds at row 3554.90) and its south wall line (row 3771.68), each the peak of a median darkness profile over columns 2250-2350 and 2245-2330, peaks refined by a parabola through the three highest samples. Carried to the local frame by the sheet's fitted similarity (data/traces/gcp/sanborn_1911_v3_sheet_20_gcps.json): local E 1334.741, N -3075.265. The bearing is the parcel's and the house's (-0.58 degrees, as the draft stood it). The fit's own residual, 3.08 m RMS on its control crossings, is all that is claimed; the draft stood the building inside a rectangle fitted to its trace.
placement.symbolic_location: 1638 S. Prairie Avenue, rear: on the alley, its north wall on the 1636/1638 lot line, parcel prairie_1638 (data/street_grid/1904.json), west side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 16th to 18th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 20).

footprint.note: About the middle of the alley wall, u east (into the lot) and v north. The sheet draws the building from the alley line (pixel column 2225.6) to its east wall line (2431.53, a median darkness profile over rows 3575-3755) and from its north wall line, on the lot line (row 3554.29), to its south wall line (3771.68), each the peak of a median darkness profile: 205.9 by 217.4 pixels at the sheet's 0.050779 m a pixel, 10.457 m deep by 11.039 m along the alley. The draft had stood it inside a rectangle fitted to its trace s20fp-1638-b2 (about 10.4 by 11.0 m).

stories.note: '2' lettered on the building: two storeys.

construction.note: Drawn pink, the sheet's colour for brick, with wall thicknesses lettered '12 12' (inches, the first storey's and the second's, as the key reads them) inside its north wall and again inside its south wall. Robinson's 1886 plate also colours it pink, its brick.

value.note: Everything but the plan, the storeys, the brick, the fire-wall end and the sheet's two window marks is RECONSTRUCTED from the K12 kit (L-k12-coach-house-kit-2320), recorded as L-k12-1638-stable-1932. The sheet gives the outline, '2' storeys, the brick, walls '12 12', a stable's X, the key's fire-wall sign at the alley end of its north wall and of its south wall, a dashed partition 1.32 m inside the east wall, and two of the key's window marks: on the alley wall about 5.67 m from the north wall line and 5.37 m from the south with a dot for each storey (openings in both storeys there), and on the north wall about 7.69 m from the alley line with one dot (an opening in one storey, built in the first as 1612's and 1620's one-dot marks are). The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (`mirror`): its party wall stands at the south end, which carries no window, and rises the kit's 0.45 m above the roof (the sheet's fire-wall sign; 1700-1706's stable stands 1.9 m south of it, past the lot line); its open gable at the north end, on the 1636/1638 lot line over 1636's open rear yard, carries the sheet's one-dot mark. The sheet's fire-wall sign at the north end is not built: the kit has one party wall and one open gable, and the north end is the one with a window in it. Every opening's s counts from the party wall's inner face (the alley and yard walls' s from the south end and the north end respectively, as the kit lays them in mirror image; the gable's from the alley face). The alley mark is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it, centred where it stands (s 5.04); the carriage bay (3.0 m clear) with the loft hatch over it toward the south end, and a man door with a loft sash over it toward the north end, are the kit's. The yard wall has a door onto the workyard at its middle between two stable sash and two loft sash; the north gable one stable sash where the sheet's mark stands and nothing over it. A gable roof with its ridge along the alley at 30 degrees over the 10.46 m span, as the deep stables (1612, 1616, 1626, 1628, 1700, 1720, 1726, 1736) took, about 3.0 m from eave to ridge. No external stair, ramp, lean-to, wing or ventilator: the sheet draws none. Not built: the dashed partition (inside) and the sheet's solid dot inside the building about 1.3 m from its south wall and 4.7 m from the alley, the key's sign for a vertical steam boiler (the kit has no stack, and the sheet draws none). The workyard is paved from the yard door to the 1638 house's rearmost wall line on the trace, 9.42 m east of the yard wall.

coach_house.note: The building's dimensions are the footprint's (inferred, above); its openings, roof and workyard are the kit's, laid out for this lot with the sheet's window mark where it puts them, and RECONSTRUCTED. See the value's own note for each choice and what bounds it.

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws the building crossed by one X, the key's sign for a stable (the T-1840 census: '2-storey brick stable (X) on the alley', s20-1638-r1), and Robinson's 1886 plate 10 crosses the brick building it draws on the same ground behind lot 1, the atlas's stable. Carried to 1904 between the two, INFERRED; no source names a horse or a carriage on this lot.

research_note: T-1932 refines the district draft (T-2334) in place under the same id onto the K12 coach-house kit. The sheet census (census row s20-1638-r1, trace s20fp-1638-b2) carries the building into 1904; the draft rules now skip that row. The two-storey brick stable is 11.04 m along the alley by 10.46 m deep, its north wall on the 1636/1638 lot line, which the sheet runs on east from it over 1636's open rear yard, and its south wall 1.9 m short of 1700-1706's stable on the 1638/1700 lot line. The kit is built in MIRROR IMAGE (as 1612's and 1726's are): its party wall at the south end, its open gable to the north, where the sheet's one-dot window mark stands on the north wall near the yard end. The sheet's window mark on the alley wall, near its middle, is built as a stable sash with a loft sash over it. Robinson's 1886 plate draws a crossed brick stable of about the same size on the same ground behind lot 1 (1638 in its margin), so it stood from before 1886 through 1911. No picture of it is known, so it has no image gate. The reading is in docs/RESEARCH/k12-1638-stable-1932/README.md.
